title: The 7-Year Bond Bear Market: Why It’s Not Done Yet
speaker: Tim Knight

macro_themes.view: TLT is in year seven of a bear market and it won't be the last year; war-driven rate shock aborted a rates top.
30-year at a data-set high, 10-year at 2007 levels, 2-year near 5%; mortgages above 7% and BBB yields ~6.2%.

calls.reason: Grinding bear market since 2020 with a dramatic breakdown to multi-year lows; long-term futures chart says year seven will not be the final year.
calls.quote: I don't think that year seven of this bond bear market will be the final year by any stretch.

calls.reason: Inverse head and shoulders from the 2020 1.2% low led to an explosive move to new multi-decade highs.
calls.quote: this is as high as it's been in this entire data set. So, this is a new multi-decade high.

calls.reason: At levels last seen in 2007 and above the recent green horizontal; rates across the curve broke out because of the war and he expects them to eventually beat prior highs.
calls.quote: I think we're on our way to beating even those rates, ultimately.

notes: Quote on beating 1980s rates was said about the 2-year but framed for rates generally. No date stated; listing Oct 4.
